## Summary

The Svelte `#each` block parsing lives in `/workspace/repo/crates/biome_html_parser/src/syntax/svelte.rs`, and the paren-handling bug you suspect is real — it lives in the lexer at `/workspace/repo/crates/biome_html_parser/src/lexer/mod.rs`. Nested parentheses inside an each-key expression break bracket tracking.

## 1. Parser file & functions (each block + each key)

File: `/workspace/repo/crates/biome_html_parser/src/syntax/svelte.rs`

- `parse_each_block` (line 157) — top-level `{#each ...}...{/each}` driver.
- `parse_each_opening_block` (line 297) — bumps `each` with `RestrictedExpressionStopAt::AsOrComma`, parses the collection expression, then the binding.
- `parse_each_as_keyed_item` (line 189) — parses `as item, i (key)`; calls `parse_each_key(p).ok()` at line 227.
- `parse_each_key` (lines 233-254) — parses the `( key )` part. This is the key function:

```rust
/// Parse the `( key )` inside the `#each` block
fn parse_each_key(p: &mut HtmlParser) -> ParsedSyntax {
    if !p.at(T!['(']) {
        return Absent;
    }

    let m = p.start();
    p.bump_with_context(
        T!['('],
        HtmlLexContext::restricted_expression(RestrictedExpressionStopAt::ClosingParen),
    );

    parse_single_text_expression_content(p).or_add_diagnostic(p, |p, range| {
        p.err_builder("Expected a key expression in parentheses", range)
    });

    // Re-lex to Svelte context to recognize ',) and other tokens
    p.re_lex(HtmlReLexContext::Svelte);

    p.expect(T![')']);

    Present(m.complete(p, SVELTE_EACH_KEY))
}
```

The opening `(` is consumed by the parser, then the key text is lexed as a single `HTML_LITERAL` token using the `ClosingParen` restricted-expression context. `parse_single_text_expression_content` is defined in `/workspace/repo/crates/biome_html_parser/src/syntax/mod.rs:801`.

## 2. The paren-consuming bug (root cause)

The literal is lexed by `consume_restricted_single_text_expression` in `/workspace/repo/crates/biome_html_parser/src/lexer/mod.rs:486-552`. The relevant loop:

```rust
let is_opening_paren = |byte: u8| byte == b'(' || byte == b'[' || byte == b'{';
let is_closing_paren = |byte: u8| byte == b')' || byte == b']' || byte == b'}';

while let Some(current) = self.current_byte() {
    match current {
        _ if current == b'<' && brackets_stack == 0 => break,
        _ if is_opening_paren(current) && !kind.matches_punct(current) => {
            brackets_stack += 1;
            self.advance(1)
        }
        _ if is_closing_paren(current) && !kind.matches_punct(current) => {
            if brackets_stack == 0 {
                break;                 // reached the closing delimiter
            } else {
                brackets_stack -= 1;
                self.advance(1)
            }
        }
        _ if brackets_stack == 0 && !is_at_start_identifier(current) => {
            let should_stop = kind.matches_punct(current);
            if should_stop {
                break;
            }
            self.advance(1);
        }
        ...
        _ => {
            self.advance(1);
        }
    }
}
```

Paired with `RestrictedExpressionStopAt` in `/workspace/repo/crates/biome_html_parser/src/token_source.rs:99-124`:

```rust
pub(crate) enum RestrictedExpressionStopAt {
    AsOrComma,
    ClosingParen,   // Stops at `)`
    ThenOrCatch,
}
impl RestrictedExpressionStopAt {
    pub(crate) fn matches_punct(&self, byte: u8) -> bool {
        match self {
            Self::AsOrComma => byte == b',',
            Self::ClosingParen => byte == b')',
            Self::ThenOrCatch => false,
        }
    }
    ...
}
```

Why nested parens break: in `ClosingParen` mode, `matches_punct(b')')` is `true`, so the `is_closing_paren(current) && !kind.matches_punct(current)` arm is **disabled for `)`** (the `!matches_punct` guard fails). Consequently:

- A `(` (e.g. from `toString(` or `key(`) hits the opening arm and increments `brackets_stack`.
- The matching inner `)` never reaches the closing arm (guard excludes it) and, because `brackets_stack != 0`, also skips the `brackets_stack == 0 && !is_at_start_identifier` stop arm, falling through to the catch-all `_ => self.advance(1)`. So `brackets_stack` is **never decremented**.
- `brackets_stack` stays `> 0`, so the real terminating `)` of the each-key is also swallowed by the catch-all instead of stopping the literal — the lexer keeps consuming past the intended key (into `}` and beyond).

For the simple case `(item.id)` it works only because `brackets_stack` stays `0` and the first `)` hits the `brackets_stack == 0 && !is_at_start_identifier` → `should_stop` break. Any nested `()` such as `(item.toString())` or `(key(item))` breaks it.

## Summary

I fixed the parser bug for Svelte list-rendering (`#each`) blocks whose key expression contains nested parentheses (a method call like `number.toString()` or a function call with an argument like `key(number)`).

### Root cause

In `crates/biome_html_parser/src/lexer/mod.rs`, `consume_restricted_single_text_expression` tracks nested brackets while lexing the key expression. The closing-bracket arm had a guard `!kind.matches_punct(current)`. In `ClosingParen` mode the stop punctuation *is* `)`, so `matches_punct(b')')` was `true`, which **disabled the closing-bracket arm for every `)`**. As a result:

- An inner `(` incremented `brackets_stack`, but the matching inner `)` fell through to the catch-all and never decremented it.
- `brackets_stack` stayed `> 0`, so the real terminating `)` of the each-key was swallowed too, and the lexer ran past the key into `}` and beyond — producing parse errors.

Simple keys like `(item.id)` worked only because the stack stayed at 0.

### Fix

Removed the `!kind.matches_punct` guard from the closing-bracket arm so it always runs. It now decrements the stack for a nested closing bracket (`brackets_stack > 0`) and only breaks at `brackets_stack == 0` — which is exactly the outer delimiter / stop punctuation. This is behavior-neutral for the other modes (`AsOrComma`, `ThenOrCatch`), since their stop punctuation is never a bracket.

### Verification

- All 161 existing `biome_html_parser` Svelte tests still pass.
- A temporary in-crate test (since removed) confirmed both target inputs now parse with **zero diagnostics** and the tree captures the full key text (`number.toString()` and `key(number)`).

Per the CRITICAL instruction, I made no changes under `tests/` — the test input and snapshot files will be applied by the verification system. The fix is source-only, isolated to the lexer.

One note: this is a user-facing parser bugfix, so a Biome PR would normally warrant a changeset (`just new-changeset`). I didn't add one since it lives outside the source scope, but let me know if you'd like me to create it.
